nice_title: Chronic heart failure in adults: diagnosis and management

first_line_treatment.notes: Titrate to maximum tolerated dose. One of 4 first-line drugs per NICE NG106 (2023 update)
Start low, titrate slowly. Do not initiate during acute decompensation

first_line_treatment.indication: All patients with HFrEF — now first-line per NICE NG106 2023 update
All patients with HFrEF — now first-line per NICE NG106 2023 update (TA902/TA929)

first_line_treatment.notes: Titrate to relieve congestion. Symptomatic, not disease-modifying

second_line_treatment.indication: Switch from ACE-I if still symptomatic on all 4 first-line drugs at max tolerated dose

additional_options.indication: ACE-I and ARB intolerant, or Afro-Caribbean patients
Sinus rhythm ≥75 bpm despite beta-blocker at max dose
Worsening symptoms despite optimal therapy, or AF rate control

monitoring: Renal function and electrolytes: before starting ACE-I/ARB/MRA, 1-2 weeks after each dose change, then 6-monthly
Weight: daily self-monitoring for fluid status
LVEF: repeat echocardiogram if clinical change or after 6-12 months of therapy
NT-proBNP/BNP: can track response to treatment
Heart rate: target <70 bpm with beta-blocker
non_pharmacological: Fluid restriction: 1.5-2L/day if hyponatraemia or fluid overload
Daily weight monitoring — report >2kg gain in 3 days
referral_criteria: New diagnosis: refer to heart failure specialist within 2 weeks
NYHA class III-IV: urgent specialist review
Consider CRT/ICD if LVEF ≤35% and QRS ≥130ms
Consider transplant if refractory to medical therapy
